splits.name: want(X) to — subject switch
splits.trigger: Does the wanting subject also do the wanted action?

outcomes.known_text: I want to speak Spanish with you now
outcomes.target_text: quiero hablar español contigo ahora

outcomes.known_text: and I want you to speak Spanish with me tomorrow
outcomes.target_text: y quiero que hables español conmigo mañana

splits.name: hope — subject switch
splits.trigger: Same question as S1, on a different matrix verb. Seeds 291 and 292 are ADJACENT: the authors put the minimal pair side by side.

outcomes.known_text: I hope I'll be able to speak better soon
outcomes.target_text: espero poder hablar mejor pronto

outcomes.known_text: I hope you'll be able to come to the party
outcomes.target_text: espero que puedas venir a la fiesta

splits.name: before / after — subject switch
splits.trigger: Same subject in the temporal clause, or a new one?

outcomes.known_text: we're friends, and after we finish I'd like to relax
outcomes.target_text: somos amigos, y después de terminar me gustaría relajarme

outcomes.known_text: are you going to help me before I have to go?
outcomes.target_text: ¿Vas a ayudarme antes de que tenga que irme?

outcomes.known_text: Do you mind if I finish my coffee before you start?
outcomes.target_text: ¿Te importa si termino mi café antes de que empieces?

outcomes.known_text: I think that he needs to consider ten possible problems
outcomes.target_text: pienso que él necesita considerar diez posibles problemas

outcomes.known_text: I don't think that she needs to sell the company
outcomes.target_text: no pienso que ella necesite vender la empresa

splits.name: relative clause — specificity
splits.trigger: Does the head noun refer to someone specific and known to exist?

outcomes.known_text: because I want to meet people who speak Spanish
outcomes.target_text: porque quiero conocer a personas que hablan español

outcomes.known_text: I don't know many people who speak Spanish
outcomes.target_text: no conozco a muchas personas que hablen español

splits.name: could → podía / pudo / podría
splits.trigger: Habitual ability in the past, a single completed event, or a hypothetical? English "could" marks none of these.

outcomes.known_text: She could write a story about that man
outcomes.target_text: ella podría escribir una historia sobre ese hombre

outcomes.known_text: he couldn't believe the three most important facts
outcomes.target_text: Él no podía creer los tres hechos más importantes

outcomes.known_text: he wasn't very patient when I couldn't answer
outcomes.target_text: Él no fue muy paciente cuando no pude contestar

outcomes.known_text: no I don't think she could this time
outcomes.target_text: no, no pienso que pueda esta vez

splits.name: the double-'d — 'd = would vs 'd = had
splits.trigger: Does the 'd sit in the main clause (= would) or the if-clause (= had)? Both spellings are 'd.

outcomes.known_text: I'd have been happy to drive if you'd told me
outcomes.target_text: habría estado encantado de conducir si me lo hubieras dicho

outcomes.known_text: I'd have driven if you'd told me how tired you were
outcomes.target_text: habría conducido si me hubieras dicho lo cansado que estabas

outcomes.known_text: if I'd known then what I know now I'd have waited
outcomes.target_text: si hubiera sabido entonces lo que sé ahora habría esperado

outcomes.known_text: if I'd known I'd have done things differently
outcomes.target_text: si lo hubiera sabido habría hecho las cosas de otra manera

splits.name: like → dative inversion
splits.trigger: None on the known side. English SUBJ-likes-OBJ becomes Spanish OBJ-pleases-DATIVE.

outcomes.known_text: my mother likes to read
outcomes.target_text: a mi madre le gusta leer

outcomes.known_text: I'd like to be able to speak after you finish
outcomes.target_text: Me gustaría poder hablar después de que termines

splits.name: know → saber / conocer (lexical)
splits.trigger: Knowing a fact vs being acquainted with a person or place. No English trace.

outcomes.known_text: that is why he didn't know the answer
outcomes.target_text: por eso él no sabía la respuesta

outcomes.known_text: I know a young woman who knows your sister
outcomes.target_text: conozco a una mujer joven que conoce a tu hermana

splits.name: ask → preguntar / pedir (lexical)
splits.trigger: Asking a question vs asking for a thing. No English trace.

outcomes.known_text: I wanted to ask you something yesterday
outcomes.target_text: quería preguntarte algo ayer

outcomes.known_text: they wanted to ask for help
outcomes.target_text: querían pedir ayuda

splits.name: personal 'a'
splits.trigger: Is the direct object a specific person? Then Spanish mints an `a` with no English trace at all.

outcomes.known_text: because I want to meet people who speak Spanish
outcomes.target_text: porque quiero conocer a personas que hablan español

outcomes.known_text: but I have to take my mother to the doctor
outcomes.target_text: pero tengo que llevar a mi madre al médico

splits.name: it is → ser / estar
splits.trigger: An inherent property vs a state or location.

outcomes.known_text: It's useful to start talking as soon as you can
outcomes.target_text: Es útil empezar a hablar lo antes posible

outcomes.known_text: It's under the bridge
outcomes.target_text: está debajo del puente
